text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland says motorcycle gangs will be forbidden to have club houses in residential areas after a woman passer-by died in a bomb explosion which destroyed the headquarters of the Bandidos, one of Norway's leading biker gangs.

-The extremely wealthy in Norway pay little or no fortune tax, two leading economist at the Norwegian Business School in Bergen say. The economists suggest replacing fortune tax with higher income tax.

-Bjoern Wolrath, former head of Swedish insurance giant Skandia, says it would a step backwards for Norway's largest insurer, Storebrand, to merge with commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Wolrath says Storebrand should seek alliances with foreign companies rather than with domestic competitors. National mergers do not result in improved competitiveness, he says.

-Shares in food-based conglomerate Orkla fell on the Oslo bourse on Thursday after the company presented first tertial results. Since the beginning of the year Orkla's share price has risen by almost 40 percent. On Thursday the A stock fell 7.3 percent to 568 crowns.

-Statoil has decided to cancel a 2.2 billion deal with Norwegian shipper Fred Olsen. The state oil company had signed a letter of intent to charter one of Olsen's rigs, but decided to shelve the plans when it discovered that modification of the rig would prove to be more expensive than first estimated.

-A study by the Norwegian statistics buerau, Statistics Norway, shows income differences among the population are increasing. The gap between the rich and the poor has widened since 1991 and is not likely to narrow in the next two years, the study concludes.
